key_insight: Across PDE benchmarks, discretization-based constraints become more accurate than AD-based PINNs as nonlinearity and discontinuities increase, especially when optimization errors are a major bottleneck.
engineering_relevance: For demanding engineering PDEs, the choice of solver formulation and network architecture should shift toward discretization constraints and GNNs when boundary conditions and flow complexity are severe.
method: Compared AD-based PINNs with discretization-based constraints.
Tested a spectrum of PDEs from linear Poisson to hypersonic flows with strong discontinuities.
Decomposed errors into approximation, optimization, and truncation terms for MLP and GNN models.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports systematic experiments over a wide range of PDE difficulty, showing a consistent trend in which discretization-based constraints outperform AD as nonlinearity strengthens.
watch_item: Discretization methods introduce truncation error, so gains depend on balancing this error against reduced optimization difficulty and may not generalize to every PDE or mesh setting.
paper_title: A Systematic Analysis of Automatic Differentiation versus Discretization-based Constraints for Physics-Informed PDE Solvers
